owner_rule: Owner: 'I dont like how often there's a proposed major settlement right next to a lore-settlement that's tiny in comparison. One would assume the marked settlement is the largest one, or at least the most important one, nearby, and others are equal to them at most.' A design rule like the binding lore order, not an Earth fit.
rule: Every proposed (unmarked) town is assigned to its nearest marked place (any marked campaign place: imperial capital, major imperial city, fortified city, fortified town, imperial fort, imperial monastery) if that place is within 75 km (about twice the median nearest-town distance of 42 km). No proposed town may have a larger built-up area than the marked place it is assigned to.
method: After the existing rules (A3 strict lore order among ranked marked places; imperial capital and major cities hold the largest areas of all towns), repeat until stable: for each marked place whose largest assigned proposed town is larger, the two swap areas; then re-apply A3 and the capital rule. Pure permutation of areas: the Earth-calibrated size distribution and all totals are unchanged. The build stops with an error if any violation remains.
measured_before: Published build: about 250 proposed towns (raw 252, corrected 249) are larger than their assigned marked place, at 102 of 151 marked places.
downstream: Supply, staffing and (if staffing changes) supply-fed reach rebuilt through the chain runner and published as the default.
outputs: output/capital_term_map_20261115 (rebuilt in place; previous published state remains in git history)
superseded: Owner (15 Nov 2026): "i dont love that they're artificial swaps post-factum, the model should take them into consideration more inherently." The swap implementation (a46488c9, 9e7bcf71) was reverted before any downstream output was published; to be replaced by an inherent settlement-hierarchy size model.
